title: Candy Corn Bag

drivers.name: Holiday: Thanksgiving (event week)
drivers.evidence: Noise-adjusted effect from 2 past occurrences: x0.49 vs baseline (2023: x0.34, 2024: x0.34, 2025: x0.35); consistent and reliable.

drivers.name: Price increase: +6.0% vs regular
drivers.evidence: Past promotions show ~3–5% demand drop per 6% price hike; no promotion at this price level, so no uplift; shrink toward 1.0 due to low evidence.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 10.2. Thanksgiving reduces demand (noise-adjusted x0.49 from 2 past occurrences), and the price is up 6% vs regular. No past promotion at this price level. The classical model suggests x0.49, but this is overly pessimistic: the price increase is mild, and the holiday effect is not absolute. The 2025 Thanksgiving week (x0.35) was a dip, but the product is seasonal and often sells well in Nov. The noise-adjusted holiday effect (x0.49) is reliable. No other drivers. The classical model already incorporates the event, so we adjust only for the price. A 6% price hike typically reduces demand by ~3–5% for this product (based on past promotions). We shrink the uplift toward 1.0 due to thin evidence. Final median: x0.49 × 0.97 = x0.475. Spreads remain 1.0 (no new uncertainty).

It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-85% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
